title.zh: 卷二十三 列傳第四 褚淵 淵弟澄 徐嗣 王儉
title.en: Volume 23 Biographies 4: Chu Yuan, Yuan Dicheng, Xu Si, Wang Jian
title.raw: 卷二十三 列傳第四 褚淵 淵弟澄 徐嗣 王儉 Volume 23 Biographies 4: Chu Yuan, Yuan Dicheng, Xu Si, Wang Jian

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷二十三‧列傳第四

translations.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4
translations.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4

sentences.zh: 褚淵字彥回，河南陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan, styled Yanhui, was a native of Yangdi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, styled Yanhui, was a man of Yangdi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖秀之，宋太常。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiuzhi was Grand Master of Ceremonies under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuzhi had been Grand Master of Ceremonies under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父湛之，驃騎將軍，尚宋武帝女始安哀公主。

translations.literal: His father Zhanzhi was General of Rapid Cavalry and had married the Princess Shi'an Aihui, daughter of Emperor Wu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhanzhi was General of Rapid Cavalry and had married Princess Shi'an Aihui, a daughter of Emperor Wu of Song.

sentences.zh: 淵少有世譽，復尚文帝女南郡獻公主，姑姪二世相繼。

translations.literal: Yuan enjoyed a reputation from youth. He also married the Princess Xian of Nan commandery, daughter of Emperor Wen—an aunt and a niece, princesses of two generations marrying the house in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was esteemed from youth. He also married Princess Xian of Nan commandery, a daughter of Emperor Wen—so that an aunt and a niece, two generations of imperial daughters, married into the clan one after the other.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，除著作佐郎，太子舍人，太宰參軍，太子洗馬，祕書丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed equerry-in-ordinary, then in succession assistant in the Imperial Library, attendant of the heir apparent, staff officer to the grand minister, steward of the heir apparent, and secretary in the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was named equerry-in-ordinary, then served in turn as assistant in the Imperial Library, attendant of the heir apparent, staff officer on the grand minister's staff, steward of the heir apparent, and secretary in the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湛之卒，淵推財與弟，唯取書數千卷。

translations.literal: When Zhanzhi died, Yuan turned the family property over to his younger brother and kept only several thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhanzhi died, Yuan pushed the family estate to his younger brother and kept only a few thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 襲爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the noble rank as Marquis of Duxiang township.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title of Marquis of Duxiang township.

sentences.zh: 歷中書郎，司徒右長史，吏部郎。

translations.literal: He served as gentleman of the secretariat, right chief clerk of the ministry of service, and director of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman of the secretariat, right chief clerk of the ministry of service, and director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝卽位，加領太子屯騎校尉，不受。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song took the throne, he was additionally given the post of colonel of the heir apparent's encampment of rapid cavalry but declined it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Song came to the throne, Yuan was additionally offered colonel of the heir apparent's encampment of rapid cavalry; he refused.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，知東宮事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant and oversaw affairs of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant and put in charge of Eastern Palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書，尋領太子右衞率，固辭。

translations.literal: He became director of the ministry of personnel and soon after was given the additional post of right commander of the heir apparent's guard, but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of personnel and was soon offered the additional post of right commander of the heir apparent's guard; he declined firmly.

sentences.zh: 司徒建安王休仁南討義嘉賊，屯鵲尾，遣淵詣軍，選將帥以下勳階得自專決。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an, Xiu Ren, marched south to suppress the Yijia rebels, encamped at Magpie Tail, and sent Yuan to the army with authority from commanders downward to decide ranks of merit on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren marched south against the Yijia faction, encamped at Magpie Tail, and sent Yuan to the army with power from commanders on down to fix merit ranks as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 事平，加驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended he was given the additional title general of rapid cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was given the additional title general of rapid cavalry.

sentences.zh: 薛安都以徐州叛，虜頻寇淮、泗，遣淵慰勞北討衆軍。

translations.literal: Xue Andu rebelled in Xu province; the northerners raided Huai and Si again and again; Yuan was sent to comfort and review the northern punitive armies.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu rebelled in Xu province; the barbarians harried Huai and Si without cease; Yuan was sent to comfort and inspect the northern expeditionary forces.

sentences.zh: 淵還啓帝言：「盱眙以西，戎備單寡，宜更配衣。

translations.literal: On his return he memorialized the emperor, saying: 「West of Xuyi the frontier garrisons are thin and few; clothing allotments should be reinforced.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he memorialized the throne: 「West of Xuyi the frontier posts are few and weak; fresh clothing issues are needed.

sentences.zh: 汝陰、荊亭竝已圍逼，安豐又已不守，壽春衆力止足自保，若使遊騎擾壽陽，則江外危迫，歷陽、瓜步、鍾離、義陽皆須實力重戍，選有幹用者處之。

translations.literal: Ruyin and Jingting are both already besieged; Anfeng has likewise fallen; Shouchun's forces can barely hold themselves. If raiding horsemen harass Shouyang, the lands beyond the Yangtze will be pressed to peril. Liyang, Guabu, Zhongli, and Yiyang all need solid, heavy garrisons—men of real capacity should be placed there.」
translations.idiomatic: Ruyin and Jingting are both under siege; Anfeng is already lost; Shouchun has strength only to defend itself. If roaming cavalry trouble Shouyang, the south bank will be hard pressed. Liyang, Guabu, Zhongli, and Yiyang all need real troops in strong garrisons—choose men of ability and station them there.」

sentences.zh: 」帝在藩，與淵以夙素相善，及卽位，深相委寄，事皆見從。

translations.literal: While the emperor was still a prince he and Yuan had been close from long acquaintance; when he took the throne he entrusted Yuan deeply and followed his counsel in all things.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was still a prince he and Yuan had been old friends; once he reigned he leaned on Yuan in everything, and Yuan's word was always taken.

sentences.zh: 改封雩都縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Marquis of Yudu district, five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Marquis of Yudu, five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中，領右衞將軍，尋遷散騎常侍，丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant and commander of the right guard, then soon after to attendant cavalier at large and intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant and commander of the right guard, then soon after attendant cavalier at large and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 出爲吳興太守，常侍如故，增秩千石，固辭增秩。

translations.literal: He went out as administrator of Wuxing, his regular attendance unchanged, with a salary increase of one thousand shi—but firmly declined the increase.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Wuxing, retaining his regular attendance, with a raise of one thousand shi in salary—and firmly declined the raise.

sentences.zh: 明帝疾甚，馳使召淵，付以後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming grew gravely ill he sent a fast rider to summon Yuan and entrusted him with the succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was near death he sent a fast courier to summon Yuan and entrusted him with what was to come.

sentences.zh: 帝謀誅建安王休仁，淵固諫，不納。

translations.literal: The emperor plotted to execute Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren; Yuan remonstrated firmly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to kill Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren; Yuan remonstrated hard but could not turn him.

sentences.zh: 復爲吏部尚書，領常侍、衞尉如故，不受，乃授右僕射，衞尉如故。

translations.literal: He was again made director of personnel with regular attendance and commandant of the guard as before, but declined; he was then given vice director of the masters of writing with commandant of the guard unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named director of personnel with regular attendance and commandant of the guard as before, but declined; he was then given vice director of the masters of writing, commandant of the guard unchanged.

sentences.zh: 淵以母年高羸疾，晨昏須養，固辭衞尉，不許。

translations.literal: Yuan pleaded that his mother was aged and frail and needed care morning and evening, and firmly declined the commandancy of the guard, but was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said his mother was old and failing and needed him morning and night, and firmly declined the guard commandancy—but the court would not release him.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，遺詔以爲中書令、護軍將軍，加散騎常侍，與尚書令袁粲受顧命，輔幼主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, the testamentary edict named him director of the secretariat and protector of the army, with additional attendant cavalier at large, sharing the imperial charge with Director Yuan Can to assist the young sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, the death edict made him director of the secretariat and protector of the army, with additional attendant cavalier at large, sharing the regency with Director Yuan Can to assist the young emperor.

sentences.zh: 淵同心共理庶事，當奢侈之後，務弘儉約，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Yuan worked in concert at governing the myriad affairs; after an age of extravagance he pressed for thrift, and the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan governed in concert with Can; after years of excess he pressed for thrift, and the people leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 接引賔客，未嘗驕倦。

translations.literal: He received guests and never showed pride or weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed guests and never showed arrogance or fatigue.

sentences.zh: 王道隆、阮佃夫用事，姧賂公行，淵不能禁也。

translations.literal: Wang Daolong and Ruan Tianfu held power; bribery ran wild in public—and Yuan could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong and Ruan Tianfu held the reins; graft ran openly in the streets—and Yuan could not check it.

sentences.zh: 遭庶母郭氏喪，有至性，數日中，毀頓不可復識。

translations.literal: When his stepmother Lady Guo died he showed utmost filial feeling; for several days he was so shattered he could no longer be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother Lady Guo died his grief was absolute; for days he was so broken one could no longer know his face.

sentences.zh: 朞年不盥櫛，惟泣淚處乃見其本質焉。

translations.literal: For the full year of mourning he neither washed nor combed; only where tears fell could one see his true face.
translations.idiomatic: For a full year he neither bathed nor combed his hair; only where tears had washed his skin could one see him as he was.

sentences.zh: 詔斷哭，禁弔客。

translations.literal: An edict forbade wailing; guests were barred from condolence visits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cut off public mourning; condolence callers were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，起爲中軍將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: After the burial he resumed office as general of the central army, his other posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he returned to office as general of the central army, his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，桂陽王休範反，淵與衞將軍袁粲入衞宮省，鎮集衆心。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui year 2 Prince Guiyang Xiu Fan rebelled; Yuan and General of the Guard Yuan Can entered the palace to steady the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui year 2 Prince Guiyang Xiu Fan rose in rebellion; Yuan and General of the Guard Yuan Can entered the palace precincts to steady the court.

sentences.zh: 淵初爲丹陽，與從弟炤同載出，道逢太祖，淵舉手指太祖車謂炤曰：「此非常人也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan had been intendant of Danyang, he rode out with his cousin Zhuo in the same carriage and met the Grand Ancestor on the road; Yuan raised his hand toward the Grand Ancestor's carriage and said to Zhuo, 「That is no ordinary man.」
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Yuan was intendant of Danyang, he rode out with his cousin Zhuo in one carriage and met the Grand Ancestor on the road; Yuan lifted his hand toward the Grand Ancestor's carriage and said to Zhuo, 「That is no ordinary man.」

sentences.zh: 」出爲吳興，太祖餉物別，淵又謂之曰：「此人材貌非常，將來不可測也。

translations.literal: When he went out to Wuxing, the Grand Ancestor sent gifts apart from the rest; Yuan said again, 「This man's talent and bearing are extraordinary; what he will become cannot be measured.」
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan went out to Wuxing, the Grand Ancestor sent him gifts set apart from the usual; Yuan said again, 「This man's talent and bearing are out of the common run; no one can tell how far he will go.」

sentences.zh: 」及顧命之際，引太祖豫焉。

translations.literal: At the moment of the imperial charge he drew the Grand Ancestor into the arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of the regency he brought the Grand Ancestor into the council.

sentences.zh: 太祖旣平桂陽，遷中領軍，領南兖州，增戶邑。

translations.literal: After the Grand Ancestor pacified Guiyang he was transferred to central commander of the guards and given South Yan province, with an increase to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Ancestor pacified Guiyang he was made central commander of the guards and given South Yan province, with an enlarged fief.

sentences.zh: 太祖固讓，與淵及衞軍袁粲書曰：「下官常人，志不及遠。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor firmly declined and wrote to Yuan and Yuan Can, General of the Guard: 「Your subordinate is a common man whose ambitions do not reach far.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor declined firmly and wrote to Yuan and to Yuan Can, General of the Guard: 「I am a common man; my aims do not reach far.

sentences.zh: 隨運推斥，妄踐非涯，才輕任重，夙宵冰惕。

translations.literal: Dragged upward by fortune's push, I rashly tread beyond my proper place; my talent is light for a heavy burden, and morning and night I tremble on ice.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune shoved me upward and I rashly stepped past my measure; my talent is slight for a heavy charge, and morning and night I shiver as on ice.

sentences.zh: 近值國危，含氣同奮，況在下官，寧吝身命。

translations.literal: Lately the state stood in peril and men drew breath and strove as one; how much more your subordinate—could he begrudge his own life?
translations.idiomatic: Lately the realm was in peril and men held their breath and fought as one; how much less could I, your subordinate, begrudge my own life?

sentences.zh: 履冒鋒炭，報效恒理，而褒嘉之典，偏見甄沐，貴登端戎，秩加爵土，瞻言霄衢，魂神震墜。

translations.literal: I walked through fire and blade; repayment is the constant law of service—yet the rewards of praise fall skew toward me alone: exalted at the head of the army, rank and fief both increased. Looking toward heaven's road, my spirit quakes and falls.
translations.idiomatic: I walked through fire and steel; to repay service is the constant law—yet the honors of praise fall all on me alone: raised to command the army's van, rank added and fief enlarged. When I look toward heaven's road my soul shudders and falls.

sentences.zh: 下官奉上以誠，率性無矯，前後忝荷，未嘗固讓。

translations.literal: Your subordinate serves above with sincerity and follows his nature without pretense; before and after I have accepted honors and never once firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: I serve my superiors in sincerity and follow my nature without artifice; time after time I have accepted favor and never once held out in refusal.

sentences.zh: 至若今授，特深恇迫。

translations.literal: But this present appointment presses upon me with special shame.
translations.idiomatic: But this present grant presses on me with a shame all its own.

sentences.zh: 寔以銜恩先旨，義兼陵闕，識蔽防萌，宗戚構禍，引誚歸咎，旣已靦顏，乃復乘災求幸，藉亂取貴，斯實國家之恥，非臣子所忍也。

translations.literal: Truly, bearing grace from your former intent, the righteousness touches even the gates of the royal tombs; my understanding was dim and I failed to guard against the first sprout—kinsmen of the imperial clan brewed disaster and I drew blame upon myself. Already ashamed in face, I would again ride disaster to seek luck and borrow disorder for rank—that is truly the state's shame, not what a minister can bear.
translations.idiomatic: Truly I bear grace from your former charge, and duty binds me even at the tombs of the kings; my sight was dim and I did not check the first sprout—imperial kinsmen brewed calamity and I drew reproach on myself. Already shamed in the face, I would again ride calamity to seek fortune and borrow chaos for rank—that is the nation's disgrace, not what a subject can endure.

sentences.zh: 且榮不可濫，寵不可昧，乞蠲中候，請停增邑，庶保止足，輸效淮湄。

translations.literal: Glory must not be heaped up, favor must not be grasped in the dark: I beg to be released from central commander, and ask that the fief increase be halted, that I may keep to enough and offer service on the Huai's banks.
translations.idiomatic: Glory must not be piled high, favor must not be taken in the dark: I beg release from central command, and ask that the fief increase be stopped, that I may rest in sufficiency and serve on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 如使伐匈奴，凱歸反旆，以此受爵，不復固辭矣。

translations.literal: If we are to campaign against the Xiongnu and return in triumph with banners reversed, then to accept enfeoffment on that account—I will not decline again.」
translations.idiomatic: If we are to strike the northern foe and return with victory banners reversed, then to take rank on that score—I will not refuse again.」

sentences.zh: 」淵、粲荅曰：「來告颖亮，敬挹無已。

translations.literal: Yuan and Can replied: 「Your message is keen and bright; we receive it with endless respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Can answered: 「Your words are keen and clear; we receive them with unending respect.

sentences.zh: 謙貶居心，深承非飾，此誠此旨，久著言外，況復造席舒衿，迂翰緒意，推情顧己，信足書紳。

translations.literal: Humility and self-abasement dwell in your heart—we deeply accept that this is no mere show; this sincerity and this intent have long stood plain beyond words. How much more now, when you spread the mat and loosen the collar, when you defer your brush and unfold your meaning—we weigh feeling against ourselves, and faith enough could be written on silk.
translations.idiomatic: Humility lives in your heart—we know well this is no ornament; this mind and this aim have long been plain beyond speech. How much more now, when you spread your mat and open your collar, when you set down the brush and lay out your meaning—we weigh your feeling against ourselves, and trust enough to inscribe on silk.

sentences.zh: 但今之所宜商搉，必以輕重相推。

translations.literal: Yet what must be weighed now is surely the push and pull of weight against weight.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what must be weighed now is surely how weight is set against weight.

sentences.zh: 世惟多難，事屬雕弊，四維恇擾，邊氓未安，國家費廣，府藏須備，北狄侵邊，憂虞交切。

translations.literal: The age has known only many hardships; affairs are in ruin; the four cardinal bonds are unsettled; border folk are not yet at peace; state expenses run wide; the treasury must be kept stocked; northern barbarians harry the frontiers; anxieties press on every side.
translations.idiomatic: These are years of unending trouble; the realm is worn to the bone; the four pillars of rule shake; the border people have no rest; the state's costs run deep and the treasury must be kept full; the northern enemy probes the marches; worry presses from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 宇內含識，尚爲天下危心，相與共荷任寄若此，當可稍脩廉退不？

translations.literal: Men of understanding within the realm still hold the empire in anxious hearts; sharing a burden of trust such as this—could one still practice modest withdrawal?
translations.idiomatic: Every man of sense under heaven still holds his breath for the realm; carrying a trust such as this together—how could one still stand apart in humble withdrawal?

sentences.zh: 求之懷抱，實謂不可。

translations.literal: Searching one's inner heart, this truly cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Search the heart, and the answer is plain: it cannot be.

sentences.zh: 了其不可，理無固執。

translations.literal: Knowing it cannot be done, there is no reason to persist obstinately.
translations.idiomatic: Once that is understood, obstinacy has no ground to stand on.

sentences.zh: 且勍寇窮凶，勢過原燎，釁逆倉卒，終古未聞，常時懼惑，當慮先定，結壘新亭，枕戈待敵，斷決之策，寔有由然。

translations.literal: Moreover the fierce rebel was utterly vicious; his force outspread a prairie fire; sudden treachery unheard of since antiquity; at ordinary times one would fear and hesitate—but one ought to secure victory first; building fortifications at Xinting, sleeping on weapons awaiting the foe—the decisive policy indeed had its reason.
translations.idiomatic: And the rebel was fierce to the end; his power spread like fire across dry grass; treachery sprung in a day was unheard of in all former ages. At any other time fear might have frozen you—but then one had to fix the outcome first. To build walls at Xinting, to sleep on your weapons and wait for the enemy: the policy that broke the deadlock had reason enough behind it.

sentences.zh: 鋒鏑初交，元惡送首，總律制奇，判於此舉。

translations.literal: At the first clash of blades the chief villain sent his head; marshaling law and devising strategy, judgment fell in this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the first clash of steel the arch-rebel lost his head; command and stratagem met in that one blow.

sentences.zh: 裂邑萬戶，登爵槐鼎，亦何足少酬勳勞，粗塞物聽。

translations.literal: A fief of ten thousand households and elevation to noble rank—how could that be too little to repay meritorious toil; it only roughly answers public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: A fief of ten thousand households and a seat among the great offices—what is that, set against such labor? It barely answers what the world expects to hear.

sentences.zh: 今以近侍禁旅，進昇中候，乘平隨牒，取此非叨。

translations.literal: Now, from palace guard close to the throne, you are advanced to Palace Attendant; riding the season of peace according to rank—this is no undue favor.
translations.idiomatic: To rise from the inner guard by the throne to Palace Attendant, in a time when calm follows the edict—that is no stolen honor.

sentences.zh: 濟、河昔所履牧，鎮軍秩不逾本，詳校階序，愧在未優，就加沖損，特虧朝制。

translations.literal: Ji and He you once governed; the army commander rank does not exceed your original rank; on careful comparison of precedence you have not been overfavored; to seek further reduction would specially harm court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The districts of Ji and He you once held in trust; the army command does not outrank what you bore before; set the grades side by side and you are not pampered; to press for more denial would wound the court's order itself.

sentences.zh: 奉職數載，同舟無幾，劉領軍峻節霜明，臨危不顧，音迹未晞，奄成今古，迷途失偶，慟不及悲。

translations.literal: In office these several years, we were few who shared the same boat; General Liu's stern integrity was bright as frost; facing peril he did not look to self; his voice and traces are not yet cold, yet suddenly he belongs to past and present; lost on a dark road without companion—grief cannot keep pace with mourning.
translations.idiomatic: These years in office we were few who rode the same boat. General Liu's stern honor shone bright as frost; when danger came he did not turn inward. His voice is not yet cold on the air, yet already he belongs to yesterday. Grief has lost its companion on a road without signposts; sorrow cannot catch up with the loss.

sentences.zh: 戎謨內寄，恒務倍急，秉操辭榮，將復誰委？

translations.literal: Military plans are entrusted within; constant duties redouble in urgency; if one holds integrity and declines glory—on whom shall it be entrusted again?
translations.idiomatic: War is planned within these walls; the charge grows heavier by the day. If the man who holds the seal refuses honor—who is left to take it up?

sentences.zh: 誠惟軍柄所期，自增茂圭社，誓貫朝廷，匹夫里語，尚欲信厚，君令必行，逡巡何路。

translations.literal: Truly only what military authority expects: to add glory to the clan fief and oath that pierces the court; even village folk wish faith kept deep; the ruler's command must go forth—what road is there to hesitate?
translations.idiomatic: What the sword asks for is plain: more glory for your house, an oath that binds the court. Even villagers keep their word in full; when the lord commands, where is the path of delay?

sentences.zh: 凡位居物首，功在衆先，進退之宜，當與衆共。

translations.literal: In general, those at the head of things, merit before the multitude—the propriety of advance and retreat ought to be shared with all.
translations.idiomatic: Who stands first among men, whose merit leads the host—the way forward and back is never a private road.

sentences.zh: 苟殉獨善，何以處物。

translations.literal: If one would die for private virtue alone, how could one comport with the world?
translations.idiomatic: If you sought only your own goodness, how would you stand among others?

sentences.zh: 受不自私，彌見至公。

translations.literal: That acceptance is not selfish shows all the more supreme impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: To accept without grasping is the clearest sign of true impartiality.

sentences.zh: 表裏詳究，無而後可。

translations.literal: Inner and outer examined in detail—only when there is no objection may one proceed.
translations.idiomatic: We have weighed this inward and outward; only when nothing stands against it may it stand.

sentences.zh: 想體殊常，深思然納。

translations.literal: We trust you will appreciate how extraordinary this is and, pondering deeply, grant assent.
translations.idiomatic: We trust you will see how extraordinary the moment is, and after deep thought, consent.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃受命。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor thereupon accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor thereupon accepted the commission.

sentences.zh: 其年，淵加尚書令、侍中，給班劔二十人，固讓令。

translations.literal: That year Yuan was additionally appointed director of the masters of writing and palace attendant, granted twenty ceremonial swords as escort; he firmly declined the directorship.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yuan was additionally made director of the masters of writing and palace attendant, granted twenty ceremonial swords as escort; he firmly declined the directorship.

sentences.zh: 三年，進爵爲侯，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: In year 3 he was advanced in rank to marquis and his fief increased by a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was advanced to marquis and his fief increased by a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 服闋，改授中書監，侍中、護軍如故，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to palace secretary supervisor; palace attendant and protector of the army unchanged; granted a suite of ceremonial horns and drums.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made palace secretary supervisor; palace attendant and protector of the army stood as before; he was granted a suite of ceremonial horns and drums.

sentences.zh: 明年，淵後嫡母吳郡公主薨，毀瘠如初。

translations.literal: The next year Yuan's stepmother, the Princess of Wu commandery, died; his wasting grief was as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yuan's stepmother, the Princess of Wu commandery, died; his wasting grief matched the first bereavement.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，詔攝職，固辭。

translations.literal: When burial was finished, an edict ordered him to resume duties; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When burial was finished, an edict ordered him back to office; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又以朞祭禮及，表解職，並不許。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to resign his office because the first-anniversary rites had come due; both requests were denied.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to resign when the first-anniversary rites fell due; both requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧酷暴稍甚，太祖與淵及袁粲言世事，粲曰：「主上幼年微過易改，伊、霍之事，非季代所行，縱使功成，亦終無全地。

translations.literal: Cangwu's cruelty and violence grew somewhat worse; the Grand Ancestor spoke with Yuan and Yuan Can about affairs of state; Can said: "The sovereign is young; minor faults are easy to amend; affairs like Yi Yin and Huo Guang are not for an age's decline—even if they succeeded, in the end there would be no safe footing."
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu's cruelty grew sharper; the Grand Ancestor spoke with Yuan and Yuan Can about affairs of state; Can said: 「The sovereign is young; small faults are easy to mend; deeds like Yi Yin and Huo Guang belong to a fallen age—even if they succeeded, in the end there would be no safe footing for you.」

sentences.zh: 」淵默然，歸心太祖。

translations.literal: Yuan was silent; his heart turned to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was silent; his heart turned to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 及廢蒼梧，羣公集議，袁粲、劉秉旣不受任，淵曰：「非蕭公無以了此。

translations.literal: When Cangwu was deposed the assembled lords deliberated; Yuan Can and Liu Bing had already refused office; Yuan said: "Without Duke Xiao this cannot be brought to conclusion."
translations.idiomatic: When Cangwu was deposed the lords assembled in counsel; Yuan Can and Liu Bing had already refused office; Yuan said: 「Without Duke Xiao this cannot be brought to an end.」

sentences.zh: 」手取書授太祖。

translations.literal: He took the document by hand and handed it to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He took the document in hand and gave it to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「相與不肯，我安得辭！

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "When you all refuse, how can I decline!"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor said: 「When you all refuse, how can I decline!」

sentences.zh: 」事乃定。

translations.literal: The matter was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 順帝立，改號衞將軍、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun was enthroned, Yuan's title was changed to general of the guard, bearer of the staff equal to the Three Excellencies; palace attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun was enthroned, Yuan was made general of the guard, bearer of the staff equal to the Three Excellencies; palace attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 甲仗五十人入殿。

translations.literal: Fifty suit-armed attendants entered the palace hall with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty suit-armed attendants entered the palace hall with him.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，袁粲懷貳，太祖召淵謀議，淵曰：「西夏釁難，事必無成；

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Yuan Can harbored divided loyalty; the Grand Ancestor summoned Yuan for counsel; Yuan said: "The western rebellion—such affairs are doomed never to succeed;
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Yuan Can wavered in his loyalty; the Grand Ancestor summoned Yuan for counsel; Yuan said: 「The western rising is bound to fail;

sentences.zh: 公當先備其內耳。

translations.literal: Your Grace ought to prepare first within."
translations.idiomatic: Your Grace ought to secure the house within first.」

sentences.zh: 」太祖密爲其備。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor secretly made the preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor secretly made the preparations.

sentences.zh: 事平，進中書監、司空，本官如故。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Yuan was advanced to palace secretary supervisor and minister of works; his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Yuan was advanced to palace secretary supervisor and minister of works; his original offices stood as before.

sentences.zh: 淵美儀貌，善容止，俯仰進退，咸有風則。

translations.literal: Yuan had fine bearing and appearance, skilled in demeanor; in bowing, rising, advancing, and retiring—all had proper style.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had fine looks and bearing, skilled in demeanor; in bowing, rising, advancing, and retiring, all had proper style.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，百僚遠國使莫不延首目送之。

translations.literal: At every court session the hundred officials and envoys from distant states alike craned their necks and watched him depart.
translations.idiomatic: At every court session the hundred officials and envoys from distant states alike craned their necks and watched him go.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝嘗歎曰：「褚淵能遲行緩步，便持此得宰相矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song once sighed: "Chu Yuan can walk slowly and with measured steps—with just that he could win the chancellorship."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song once sighed: 「Chu Yuan can walk slowly and with measured steps—with that alone he could win the chancellorship.」

sentences.zh: 」尋加尚書令，本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made director of masters of writing; his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made director of the masters of writing; his original offices stood as before.

sentences.zh: 二年，重申前命爲司徒，又固讓。

translations.literal: In year 2 the throne again offered his former appointment as minister of works; he again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 the former appointment as minister of works was offered again; he again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 是年虜動，上欲發王公已下無官者爲軍，淵諫以爲無益實用，空致擾動，上乃止。

translations.literal: That year the northerners stirred; the sovereign wished to mobilize princes, dukes, and all below who held no office as soldiers; Yuan remonstrated that it would be of no real use and would only stir pointless commotion; the sovereign then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That year the northerners stirred; the sovereign wished to mobilize princes, dukes, and every man without office into the ranks; Yuan remonstrated that it would serve no real end and would only stir pointless unrest; the sovereign then stopped.

sentences.zh: 朝廷機事，多與諮謀，每見從納，禮遇甚重。

translations.literal: On weighty state affairs the court often consulted him; his advice was usually followed; his courtesy treatment was very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty affairs of state the court often sought his counsel; his advice was usually followed; the honor shown him was very great.

sentences.zh: 上大宴集，酒後謂羣臣曰：「卿等竝宋時公卿，亦當不言我應得天子。

translations.literal: At a great court banquet, after wine the sovereign said to the assembled ministers: "You were all ministers and high officers of Song—surely you also must think I ought to have become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: At a great court banquet, after wine the sovereign said to the ministers: 「You were all ministers of Song—surely you must also think I ought to have become Son of Heaven.」

sentences.zh: 」王儉等未及答，淵斂板曰：「陛下不得言臣不早識龍顏。

translations.literal: Wang Jian and the rest had not yet answered when Yuan clasped his tablet and said: "Your Majesty must not say your subject failed to recognize the imperial countenance early."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian and the rest had not yet answered when Yuan clasped his tablet and said: 「Your Majesty must not say your subject failed to recognize the imperial countenance early.」

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「吾有愧文叔，知公爲朱祜久矣。」

translations.literal: The sovereign laughed and said: "I am ashamed before Guangwu—that I knew you were Zhu You long ago."
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign laughed and said: 「I am ashamed before Guangwu—that I knew you were Zhu You long ago.」

sentences.zh: 淵涉獵談議，善彈琵琶。

translations.literal: Yuan ranged widely in conversation and debate, and excelled at playing the pipa.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan ranged widely in talk and debate, and excelled at the pipa.

sentences.zh: 世祖在東宮，賜淵金鏤柄銀柱琵琶。

translations.literal: When Shizu was at the Eastern Palace he bestowed on Yuan a pipa with gold-inlaid handle and silver pillars.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu was crown prince at the Eastern Palace he bestowed on Yuan a pipa with gold-inlaid handle and silver pillars.

sentences.zh: 性和雅有器度，不妄舉動，宅嘗失火，煙焰甚逼，左右驚擾，淵神色怡然，索轝來徐去。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle, refined, and possessed breadth of spirit; he never acted rashly; when his residence once caught fire and smoke and flames pressed close, those at his side panicked; Yuan's expression remained calm; he called for his carriage and departed at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was gentle and measured, never rash; when fire once pressed close on his residence, those beside him panicked; Yuan's face stayed calm; he called for his carriage and left at leisure.

sentences.zh: 輕薄子頗以名節譏之，以淵眼多白精，謂之「白虹貫日」，言爲宋氏亡徵也。

translations.literal: Frivolous men often mocked him for his sense of propriety; because Yuan's eyes showed much white, they called it "white rainbow piercing the sun" and said it was an omen of Song's fall.
translations.idiomatic: Frivolous men often mocked his sense of propriety; because his eyes showed much white they called it 「white rainbow piercing the sun」 and said it was an omen of Song's fall.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，遺詔以淵爲錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor died, the testamentary edict appointed Yuan Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor died, his testamentary edict named Yuan Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，無單拜錄者，有司疑立優策。

translations.literal: Since the dynasty south of the Yangtze began, no one had been appointed Recorder by a lone commission; the relevant offices doubted whether to establish a laudatory edict.
translations.idiomatic: No one south of the Yangtze had ever received Recorder as a sole appointment; the relevant offices were unsure whether a laudatory edict was required.

sentences.zh: 尚書王儉議，以爲「見居本官，別拜錄，推理應有策書，而舊事不載。

translations.literal: Wang Jian of the Masters of Writing submitted an opinion, saying, 「While holding his present office, he is separately appointed Recorder—in reason there should be a commissioning edict, but precedent is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian of the Masters of Writing argued: 「He still holds his present post yet is separately invested as Recorder; by right there should be a commissioning edict, but precedent does not say so.

sentences.zh: 中朝以來，三公王侯，則優策竝設，官品第二，策而不優。

translations.literal: Since the central dynasty, for Three Dukes and princes, laudatory and commissioning edicts were set up together; for rank-second officials, commissioning but no laudatory.
translations.idiomatic: Since the central court, Three Dukes and princes received laudatory and commissioning edicts together; second-rank ministers received commissioning edicts without laudatory texts.

sentences.zh: 優者褒美，策者兼明委寄。

translations.literal: Laudatory ones express praise; commissioning ones also clarify entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: The laudatory text praises merit; the commissioning edict states the charge entrusted.

sentences.zh: 尚書職居天官，政化之本，尚書令品雖第三，拜必有策。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing stand as Heaven's officials, root of government and transformation; though the Director of the Masters of Writing is rank three, on appointment there is always a commissioning edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing are Heaven's bureau and the root of rule; though the Director is only third rank, appointment always brings a commissioning edict.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書品秩不見，而總任彌重，前代多與本官同拜，故不別有策。

translations.literal: Recorder of the Masters of Writing has no listed rank, yet the overall charge is heavier; former ages mostly appointed with the base office, so there was no separate commissioning edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Recorder's rank is nowhere listed, yet his burden is greater; past ages usually invested him together with his standing office, and so issued no separate edict.

sentences.zh: 卽事緣情，不容均之凡僚，宜有策書，用申隆寄。

translations.literal: Given the matter and circumstances, he cannot be equated with ordinary officials; there should be a commissioning edict to declare the weight of the charge—
translations.idiomatic: Given the office and the man, he cannot be lumped with ordinary officials; a commissioning edict is needed to proclaim the weight of the trust—

sentences.zh: 旣異王侯，不假優文」。

translations.literal: being distinct from princes and marquises, no laudatory text is needed.」
translations.idiomatic: and as he is no prince or marquis, no laudatory text is called for.」

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 尋增淵班劔爲三十人，五日一朝。

translations.literal: Soon Yuan's ceremonial halberds were increased to thirty; he attended court every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan's train of ceremonial halberds was raised to thirty; he came to court every five days.

sentences.zh: 頃之寢疾。

translations.literal: Before long he took to his bed with illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 上相星連有變，淵憂之，表遜位。

translations.literal: The Superior Minister star showed linked changes; Yuan was troubled and memorialized to yield his post.
translations.idiomatic: The Superior Minister star showed linked disturbances; troubled, Yuan memorialized to yield his post.

sentences.zh: 又因王儉及侍中王晏口陳於世祖，世祖不許。

translations.literal: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan speak orally before Shizu; Shizu did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan plead in person before Shizu; Shizu refused.

sentences.zh: 又啓曰：「臣顧惟凡薄，福過災生，未能以正情自安，遠慚彥輔。

translations.literal: He memorialized again, saying, 「Your servant reflects on his common mediocrity—blessing has outrun merit and calamity is born; unable to settle his heart in rectitude, far ashamed before worthy counselors.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again: 「Your servant knows himself common and slight—favor has outstripped desert and trouble follows; I cannot quiet my heart in truth and am ashamed before worthy counselors.

sentences.zh: 旣內懷耿介，便覺晷刻難推。

translations.literal: Inwardly unyielding, each instant becomes hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Outward duty sits ill on an inward stiffness; hour by hour drags.

sentences.zh: 叨職未久，首歲便嬰疾篤，爾來沈痼，頻經危殆，彌深憂震。

translations.literal: Your servant bore office not long; in the first year he fell gravely ill; since then chronic ailments, passing danger again and again, worry and dread ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: I have not long held office; in the first year I was stricken gravely ill; since then lingering sickness, again and again at death's door, and dread only deepens.

sentences.zh: 陛下曲存遲回，或謂僉議同異，此出於留慈每過，愛欲其榮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bent to allow delay; some say the collective deliberations differ—this comes from lingering affection exceeding measure, love wishing him honor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has indulged my delay, or some will say the councils are divided—but this is only excess of kindness, love wishing me honor I do not merit.

sentences.zh: 臣年四十有八，叨忝若此，以疾陳遜，豈駭聽察。

translations.literal: Your servant is forty-eight, bearing such honor at fault; to cite illness and yield—is that to startle imperial hearing?
translations.idiomatic: At forty-eight, with honors heaped on me, to plead illness and withdraw—would that shock your ears?

sentences.zh: 總錄之任，江左罕授，上隣亞台，升降蓋微。

translations.literal: The charge of overall recording is rarely granted south of the Yangtze; it borders the secondary terrace, promotion and demotion scarcely distinct.
translations.idiomatic: The overall Recordership is rarely granted in our age; its holder stands next to the Secretariat itself, and between rise and fall there is little distance.

sentences.zh: 今受祿弗辭，退絀斯願，於臣名器，非曰貶少，萬物耳目，皎然共見，寧足仰延聖慮，稍垂矜惜。

translations.literal: Now to accept salary without declining, to withdraw and cut short this wish—for your servant's name and rank it is not called a belittling reduction; all eyes under heaven see it clearly—how could it merit extending imperial concern or slight pity?
translations.idiomatic: To keep the stipend and refuse to step down, to choke off this request—for my name and rank that is no real demotion; every eye under heaven sees it plain. Why should it draw your concern or the least pity?

sentences.zh: 臣若內飾廉譽，外循謙後，此則憲書行劾，刑綱是肅。

translations.literal: If your servant adorned himself inwardly with reputation for integrity and outwardly followed humility, then the statutes would move to impeachment and the penal net would be tightened.
translations.idiomatic: If I papered myself with a show of integrity while playing at humility, the statutes would impeach me and the law would tighten its net.

sentences.zh: 臣赤誠不能行，亦幽明所不宥。

translations.literal: Your servant's naked sincerity cannot perform that; neither the visible nor invisible worlds would pardon it.
translations.idiomatic: My naked heart cannot do that; neither the living nor the dead would forgive it.

sentences.zh: 區區寸心，歸啓以實。

translations.literal: This paltry inch of heart returns to declare in truth.
translations.idiomatic: In this inch of heart I lay the truth before you.

sentences.zh: 自吝寸陰，寔願方倍堯世。

translations.literal: Cherishing each inch of shadow, truly wishing to match doubled the era of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Grudging every inch of daylight, I would only wish to serve twice the years of Yao's age.

sentences.zh: 昔王弘固請，乃於司徒爲衞將軍，宋氏行之不疑，當時物無異議，以臣方之，曾何足說。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Hong firmly petitioned and became Defender-General under the Minister of Works; the Song house did it without doubt and none objected—compared with your servant, how could words suffice?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong once pressed his plea and was made Defender-General under the Minister of Works; the Song court granted it without a murmur. Set beside me, what is my case worth speaking of?

sentences.zh: 伏願恢闡宏猷，賜開亭造，則臣死之日，猶生之年。

translations.literal: Bowing head, hoping to broaden great design, grant opening and release—then the day of your servant's death would still be as a day of life.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to widen your great design and grant me leave; then the day I die would still count as a day I lived.

sentences.zh: 」乃改授司空，領驃騎將軍，侍中、錄尚書如故。

translations.literal: 」He was then reassigned Minister of Works, with Supernal General, Palace Attendant and Recorder unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was then reassigned Minister of Works, retaining Supernal General, Palace Attendant, and Recorder as before.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍中王晏黃門郎王秀之問疾。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to ask after his health.

sentences.zh: 薨，家無餘財，負債至數十萬。

translations.literal: He died; the household had no surplus wealth, debts running to hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the family left no surplus, and debts ran into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司徒奄至薨逝，痛怛慟懷，比雖尪瘵，便力出臨哭。

translations.literal: An edict said, 「The Minister of Works suddenly reached death's end; grief and anguish pierce the heart. Though lately wasting ill, I went in person to mourn at his bier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, 「The Minister of Works has suddenly died; grief wounds the heart. Though lately I have been ill and frail, I went myself to mourn at his bier.

sentences.zh: 給東園祕器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢二十萬，布二百疋，蠟二百斤。」

translations.literal: Granted eastern garden secret coffinware, one set court robes, one suit of clothing, two hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts cloth, two hundred jin wax.」
translations.idiomatic: Grant eastern-garden funerary coffinware, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, two hundred thousand in cash, two hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.」

sentences.zh: 時司空掾屬以淵未拜，疑應爲吏敬不？

translations.literal: At the time the Minister of Works' clerks and subordinates, because Yuan had not yet taken the appointment, doubted whether they should perform the clerk's mourning obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works' aides and clerks, because Yuan had not yet formally accepted the new post, debated whether they owed him the mourning due a serving master.

sentences.zh: 王儉議：「依《禮》，婦在塗，聞夫家喪，改服而入。

translations.literal: Wang Jian's opinion: 「According to the Rites, when a wife is on the road and hears of bereavement in her husband's house, she changes garments and enters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian ruled: 「The Rites say that if a wife is still on the road when she learns of death in her husband's house, she changes her dress and enters mourning—

sentences.zh: 今掾屬雖未服勤，而吏節稟於天朝，宜申禮敬。

translations.literal: Now though the clerks have not yet served in office, their clerk's norms are received from the celestial court; they should observe ritual obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: these clerks have not yet entered active service, yet their obligations as officers come from the throne; they should observe full ritual mourning.

sentences.zh: 」司徒府史又以淵旣解職，而未恭後授，府猶應上服以不？

translations.literal: 」The Minister of Works' house clerks further argued that since Yuan had left office but the later appointment had not yet been received with ceremony, should the bureau still don mourning garb?
translations.idiomatic: 」The Minister of Works' clerks asked further: Yuan had resigned his post but had not yet been invested in the successor office—should the bureau still wear mourning?

sentences.zh: 儉又議：「依中朝士孫德祖從樂陵遷爲陳留，未入境，卒，樂陵郡吏依見君之服，陳留迎吏依娶女有吉日齊衰弔，司徒府宜依居官制服。」

translations.literal: Wang Jian again opined: 「According to the central dynasty, when scholar-official Sun Dezhi moved from Leling to Chenliu and died before entering the border, Leling county clerks wore mourning as for a present lord, Chenliu welcoming clerks wore the qi mourning of wedding-with-auspicious-day condolence; the Minister of Works' bureau should follow mourning as while in office.」
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian ruled again: 「In the central court era, when Sun Dezhi was transferring from Leling to Chenliu and died before crossing the border, Leling's clerks mourned him as their serving lord, while Chenliu's welcoming clerks wore only the abbreviated qi mourning of a betrothal condolence. The Minister of Works' house should mourn as for an officer still in office.」

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「夫褒德所以紀民，慎終所以歸厚。

translations.literal: Another edict said, 「To ennoble virtue is how the people are recorded; to be careful at the end is how thickness is returned.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, 「To honor the worthy is to teach the people; to care for the dead is to repay the living.

sentences.zh: 前王盛典，咸必由之。

translations.literal: The great codes of former kings all passed through this.
translations.idiomatic: Every great king's canon rested on this.

sentences.zh: 故侍中、司徒、錄尚書事、新除司空、領驃騎將軍、南康公淵，履道秉哲，鑒識弘曠。

translations.literal: The late Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, newly appointed Minister of Works, Supernal General, Duke of Nankang Yuan—tread the Way, held wisdom, discernment broad and far.
translations.idiomatic: The late Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, newly appointed Minister of Works, Supernal General, Duke of Nankang—Yuan—walked the Way and held wisdom; his discernment was broad and far.

sentences.zh: 爰初弱齡，清風夙舉。

translations.literal: From first weak years, pure wind early raised.
translations.idiomatic: From youth a pure reputation rose early.

sentences.zh: 登庸應務，具瞻允集。

translations.literal: Ascended to service, answered affairs, all gazes rightly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Called to office, he answered every charge; all eyes settled on him with trust.

sentences.zh: 孝友著於家邦，忠貞彰於亮采。

translations.literal: Filial piety and friendship shown in family and state, loyalty and steadfastness manifest in bright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At home filial love shone; in service loyalty stood clear in bright conduct.

sentences.zh: 佐命先朝，經綸王化，契闊屯夷，綢繆終始。

translations.literal: Assisted the mandate of the former court, wove royal transformation, through hardship and peril, intimate from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted the former throne and wove the age's governance, through reversals and hardship, bound to its course from first to last.

sentences.zh: 總錄機衡，四門惟穆，諒以同規往古，式範來今。

translations.literal: Overall recorded the pivots, four gates all serene—truly matching past ancients, model for those to come.
translations.idiomatic: As overall Recorder he steadied the pivots of state; the four gates were calm. He matched the ancients and set a measure for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 謙光彌遠，屢陳降挹，權從高旨，用虧大猷。

translations.literal: Humility's light ever farther, repeatedly declared lowering withdrawal, power followed high intent, thus diminishing great design.
translations.idiomatic: His humility ran ever deeper; again and again he asked to be lowered, and the throne, bending to his request, let a great design fall short.

sentences.zh: 將登上列，永翼聲教。

translations.literal: About to ascend the upper ranks, forever winging the sound of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of higher honors, to wing the court's teachings for long years—

sentences.zh: 天不憖遺，奄焉薨逝，朕用震慟于厥心。

translations.literal: Heaven not sparing him, suddenly perished; We are shaken and grieved in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: when Heaven, not sparing him, took him suddenly. We are shaken to the core.

sentences.zh: 其贈公太宰，侍中、錄尚書、公如故。

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously enfeoffed Duke Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant and Recorder and Duke as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoff him as Duke and Grand Preceptor; let Palace Attendant, Recorder, and ducal rank stand as before.

sentences.zh: 給節，加羽葆鼓吹，增班劔爲六十人。

translations.literal: Grant credentials; add feather-canopy and drum-and-pipe escort; increase ceremonial halberds to sixty men.
translations.idiomatic: Grant the credentials of office, add feather-canopy band and drum-and-pipe escort, and raise his ceremonial halberds to sixty.

sentences.zh: 葬送之禮，悉依宋太保王弘故事。

translations.literal: Burial and escort rites were entirely according to the precedent of Song Grand Tutor Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral and escort rites followed in full the precedent set for Song Grand Tutor Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 謚曰文簡。

translations.literal: The posthumous name was Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 」先是庶姓三公轜車，未有定格。

translations.literal: 」 Earlier, light carriages for Three Dukes of commoner origin had no fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: 」 Until then, the open carriages of commoner-born Three Dukes had never had a fixed standard.

sentences.zh: 王儉議官品第一，皆加幢絡，自淵始也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian argued that all officials of the first rank should add canopy tassels—beginning with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian held that every first-rank minister should bear canopy tassels on his carriage; the custom began with Yuan.

sentences.zh: 又詔淵妻宋故巴西主埏隧蹔啓，宜贈南康郡公夫人。

translations.literal: Another edict: Yuan's wife, the former Princess of Brazil of Song, had briefly opened the tomb; she should be granted the title Lady of the Duke of Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict: Yuan's wife, once Princess of Brazil under Song, had briefly opened the tomb; she was to receive the title Lady of the Duke of Nankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 蓁字茂緒。

translations.literal: Chen styled Maoxu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Maoxu.

sentences.zh: 永明中，解褐爲員外郎，出爲義興太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he left office for the first time as Attendant Outer, then went out as Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongming he first took office as an outer attendant, then went out as Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 八年，改封巴東郡侯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his fief was changed to Marquis of Badong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Badong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 明年，表讓封還賁子霽，詔許之。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized to yield the fief and return it to his elder brother Ben's son Ji; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to surrender the fief and restore it to Ji, son of his elder brother Ben; the throne granted it.

sentences.zh: 建武末，爲太子詹事，度支尚書，領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Late in Jianwu he served as Crown Prince Household Mentor, Minister of Revenue, and Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu he was Crown Prince Household Mentor, Minister of Revenue, and Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，卒，贈太常，謚穆。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he died; posthumously he was made Minister of Ceremonies, posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 1 he died; the court posthumously made him Minister of Ceremonies and gave him the posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 淵弟澄。

translations.literal: Yuan's younger brother Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's younger brother Cheng.

sentences.zh: 淵弟 澄

translations.literal: Yuan's younger brother Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's younger brother Cheng

sentences.zh: 時東陽徐嗣，醫術妙。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Si of Dongyang was masterful in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Si of Dongyang was a physician of rare skill.

sentences.zh: 有一傖父冷病積年，重茵累褥，牀下設鑪火，猶不差。

translations.literal: A northern settler had suffered a chronic cold ailment for years—layered quilts and piled mattresses, a brazier set beneath the bed—and still did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: A northern settler had lain for years with a chronic cold ailment, buried under quilt upon quilt with a brazier beneath the bed, and still found no relief.

sentences.zh: 嗣爲作治，盛冬月，令傖父髁身坐石，啓以百瓶水，從頭自灌。

translations.literal: Si treated him; in deep winter he made the man sit naked on stone, opened a hundred bottles of water, and poured it over him from the head down.
translations.idiomatic: Si took the case. In the depth of winter he had the man sit bare on stone, broke open a hundred bottles of water, and poured them over his head.

sentences.zh: 初與數十瓶，寒戰垂死，其子弟相守垂泣，嗣令滿數。

translations.literal: After the first few dozen bottles he shivered as if near death; his sons and brothers stood by weeping, but Si ordered the full count.
translations.idiomatic: After the first few dozen bottles he shook as though dying; his kin wept at his side, but Si insisted on the full measure.

sentences.zh: 得七八十瓶後，舉體出氣如雲蒸，嗣令徹牀去被，明日立能起行，云此大熱病也。

translations.literal: After seventy or eighty bottles vapor rose from his whole body like steam; Si had the bed stripped and the covers removed, and the next day he could rise and walk at once—Si said it was a great heat illness.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy or eighty bottles steam rolled off his body; Si had bed and covers taken away, and by the next day the man could stand and walk—this, Si said, was a raging heat illness.

sentences.zh: 又春月出南籬門戲，聞笪屋中有呻吟聲，嗣曰：「此病甚重，更二日不治，必死。

translations.literal: Again, one spring day he went out to play by the South Hedge Gate and heard groaning from a bamboo-mat hut; Si said, 「This illness is very grave; if it is not treated within two days, he will die.
translations.idiomatic: Another spring day he strolled out by the South Hedge Gate and heard groaning from a mat-walled hut. Si said, 「The case is grave; without treatment within two days, the man will die.

sentences.zh: 」乃往視。

translations.literal: 」 Then he went to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: 」 He went in to see.

sentences.zh: 一姥稱舉體痛，而處處有黑無數，嗣還煮升餘湯送令服之，姥服竟，痛愈甚，跳投牀者無數，須臾，所處皆拔出長寸許，乃以膏塗諸瘡口，三日而復，云此名釘疽也。

translations.literal: An old woman said her whole body ached and black spots were everywhere without number; Si went back, boiled more than a sheng of decoction and sent it for her to drink. When she had finished, the pain grew worse; she leaped and threw herself on the bed again and again; in a moment every spot had drawn out to more than an inch; then he smeared ointment on the sores, and in three days she recovered—he said the name of the illness was nail carbuncle.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman complained of pain throughout her body and countless black spots. Si returned, brewed more than a sheng of medicine, and sent it for her to drink. When the draught was done the pain sharpened; she flung herself on the bed again and again; then every spot drew out to over an inch. He salved the wounds, and in three days she was well—he called the disease nail carbuncle.

sentences.zh: 事驗甚多，過於澄矣。

translations.literal: Verified cases were many, surpassing Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: His cures were many and proved, and he outdid Cheng.

sentences.zh: 王儉字仲寶，琅琊臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, styled Zhongbao, was a man of Langye, Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, styled Zhongbao, came from Langye, Linyi.

sentences.zh: 祖曇首，宋右光祿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tanshou was Song Right Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tanshou had been Song Right Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 父僧綽，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Sengchuo was Household Minister with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengchuo was Household Minister with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 儉生而僧綽遇害，爲叔父僧虔所養。

translations.literal: Jian was born after Sengchuo met with violence and was reared by his uncle Sengqian.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was born after Sengchuo was killed and was raised by his uncle Sengqian.

sentences.zh: 數歲，襲爵豫章侯，拜受茅土，流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: At several years of age he inherited the marquisate of Yuzhang; when he received the fief soil he wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: Still a child, he inherited the marquisate of Yuzhang; at the rite of receiving the fief soil he wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 幼有神彩，專心篤學，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: As a boy he had spirit and color; he devoted himself to earnest study and never laid his book aside.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was bright and striking; he studied with single-minded devotion and never let his books leave his hand.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹袁粲聞其名，言之於明帝，尚陽羨公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Yuan Can, Administrator of Danyang, heard his name and spoke of him to Emperor Ming; he married Princess Yangxian and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can, Administrator of Danyang, heard of him and commended him to Emperor Ming; he married Princess Yangxian and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 帝以儉嫡母武康公主同太初巫蠱事，不可以爲婦姑，欲開塚離葬，儉因人自陳，密以死請，故事不行。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jian's stepmother, Princess Wukang, was implicated in the Taichu witchcraft affair and could not stand as mother-in-law to the princess, wished to open the tomb for separate burial; Jian had someone speak for him and secretly begged with his life—the precedent was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because Jian's stepmother Princess Wukang had been caught up in the Taichu witchcraft scandal and could not face the princess as a mother-in-law, wished to open the tomb for separate burial. Jian had an intermediary plead for him and secretly offered his life in petition—the court did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 解褐祕書郎，太子舍人，超遷祕書丞。

translations.literal: He left office for Secretary, Crown Prince Attendant, and was promoted in one step to Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Secretary, then Crown Prince Attendant, and was promoted at a stroke to Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 上表求校墳籍，依《七略》撰《七志》四十卷，上表獻之，表辭甚典。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to collate the tomb archives; following the Seven Summaries he compiled the Seven Records in forty juan, memorialized and presented them—the memorial's diction was very classical.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to collate the tomb archives; following the Seven Summaries he compiled the Seven Records in forty juan and presented them with a memorial whose prose was finely classical.

sentences.zh: 又撰定《元徽四部書目》。

translations.literal: He also drew up the Yuankui Four-Part Bibliography.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Yuankui Four-Part Bibliography.

sentences.zh: 母憂，服闋爲司徒右長史。

translations.literal: After his mother's mourning, when the term ended he became Right Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he became Right Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 《晉令》，公府長史著朝服，宋大明以來著朱衣。

translations.literal: The Jin statutes: a chief clerk of a ducal or princely household wore court dress; since Song's Daming era they had worn vermillion robes.
translations.idiomatic: Jin law required a ducal chief clerk to wear court dress; since Song's Daming reign they had worn vermillion robes instead.

sentences.zh: 儉上言宜復舊，時議不許。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized that the old rule should be restored; the court at the time would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued the old custom should return; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧暴虐，儉憂懼，告袁粲求出，引晉新安主婿王獻之爲吳興例，補義興太守。

translations.literal: When Cangwu turned savage, Jian grew fearful; he told Yuan Can he wished to leave the capital, citing the Jin precedent of Wang Xianzhi, son-in-law of the Prince of Xin'an, who went to Wu Commandery, and was appointed Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cangwu grew cruel, Jian was afraid; he told Yuan Can he wished to leave the capital, citing how Wang Xianzhi, the Prince of Xin'an's son-in-law, had gone out to Wu in Jin times, and was posted as Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 還爲黃門郎，轉吏部郎。

translations.literal: He returned as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then shifted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He came back as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then moved to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，遷長兼侍中，以父終此職，固讓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he was promoted to Chief Clerk while also serving as Attendant-in-Ordinary; because his father had died in that office, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 he was made Chief Clerk while also Attendant-in-Ordinary; his father had died in that post, and he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 上壞宋明帝紫極殿，以材柱起宣陽門。

translations.literal: The emperor demolished Emperor Ming of Song's Hall of Purple Apex and used its timbers to raise the Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tore down Emperor Ming of Song's Hall of Purple Apex and used its timbers to build the Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 儉與褚淵及叔父僧虔連名上表諫曰：「臣聞德者身之基，儉者德之輿。

translations.literal: Jian, with Chu Yuan and his uncle Sengqian, jointly memorialized in remonstrance, saying: 「We have heard that virtue is the root of the person and frugality the carriage of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Chu Yuan, and his uncle Sengqian submitted a joint memorial of remonstrance: 「We have heard that virtue is the body's foundation and frugality the carriage in which virtue rides.

sentences.zh: 春臺將立，晉卿秉議，北宮肇構，漢臣盡規。

translations.literal: When the Spring Terrace was about to rise, Jin ministers held to their counsel; when the Northern Palace was first built, Han officials all laid out their rules.
translations.idiomatic: When the Spring Terrace was to be raised, ministers of Jin spoke their minds; when the Northern Palace was first built, Han officials all laid down their rule.

sentences.zh: 彼二君者，或列國常侯，或守文中主，尚使諫諍在義卽悅，況陛下聖哲應期，臣等職司隆重，敢藉前誥，竊乃有心。

translations.literal: Those two rulers were either a feudal lord of a lesser state or a sovereign who kept to the middle way, yet remonstrance in accord with right still pleased them—how much more under Your Majesty, sage and timely, while we hold weighty office: we dare borrow the words of old and venture our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Those two rulers were only a feudal lord among states or a sovereign who held the middle course, yet frank counsel in the name of right still won their assent—how much more under Your Majesty, sage and timely, when we bear grave office: we dare take the admonitions of old and lay bare our hearts.

sentences.zh: 陛下登庸宰物，節省之教旣昭，龍袞琁極，簡約之訓彌遠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ascended to order the world; teachings of thrift are already clear, yet dragon robes and jade finials make the lesson of simplicity seem ever farther away.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has taken the throne to govern all beneath Heaven; the teaching of thrift is already proclaimed, yet dragon robes and jade regalia make the lesson of simplicity seem to recede ever further.

sentences.zh: 乾華外構，采椽不斲，紫極故材，爲宣陽門，臣等未譬也。

translations.literal: Outside, the Qianhua is newly built and unhewn rafters are left uncut, yet old timber from Purple Apex is made into the Xuanyang Gate—we your ministers do not understand it.
translations.idiomatic: Without, the Qianhua is newly raised and its rafters left unshaped, yet timber from the old Purple Apex is turned into the Xuanyang Gate—we cannot make sense of it.

sentences.zh: 夫移心疾於股肱，非良醫之美；

translations.literal: To shift the mind's illness onto the arms and legs is not the mark of a good physician;
translations.idiomatic: To shift the sickness of the heart onto arms and legs is not what a good physician does;

sentences.zh: 畏影迹而馳騖，豈靜處之方？

translations.literal: to fear one's shadow and gallop in flight is not the way to dwell in stillness.
translations.idiomatic: to fear one's shadow and run in panic is not the way to abide in quiet.

sentences.zh: 且又三農在日，千畛咸事，輟望歲之勤，興土木之役，非所以宣昭大猷，光示遐邇。

translations.literal: Moreover the three cultivations are in season and a thousand fields are at work; to halt the labor that watches for the harvest and raise a task of earth and wood is not how to proclaim the great design and show it to far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the three cultivations are in their season and every furrow has its work; to set aside the toil that waits on the year's grain and launch a work of earth and timber is not how to proclaim the great design to the distant and the near.

sentences.zh: 若以門居宮南，重陽所屬，年月稍久，漸就淪胥，自可隨宜脩理而合度，改作之煩，於是乎息。

translations.literal: If the gate stands south of the palace and belongs to the yang of the Double Ninth, and with years it has gradually fallen into ruin, one may repair it as fit and to measure—then the trouble of rebuilding may cease.
translations.idiomatic: If the gate lies south of the palace in the domain of the Double Ninth, and with the years it has slowly decayed, it may be repaired as occasion requires and to proper measure—then the burden of rebuilding will end.

sentences.zh: 所啓謬合，請付外施行。

translations.literal: What we have set forth, though it may err, accords with principle; we beg it be sent out for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: What we submit may be mistaken, yet we believe it accords with right; we beg that it be sent out for action.

sentences.zh: 」上手詔酬納。

translations.literal: 」The sovereign then issued an edict accepting and praising it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor then issued an edict thanking him and taking his counsel.

sentences.zh: 宋世外六門設竹籬，是年初，有發白虎樽者，言「白門三重門，竹籬穿不完」。

translations.literal: Outside the palace's six gates in Song times the city had bamboo fences; at the beginning of that year someone broke open a White Tiger casket, saying, 「White Gate's triple gates—bamboo fences cannot pierce them through.」
translations.idiomatic: In Song times bamboo fences stood outside the capital's six palace gates. Early that year someone broke open a White Tiger wine jar and read the omen: 「The White Gate's triple gates—the bamboo fences will never pierce through.」

sentences.zh: 上感其言，改立都墻。

translations.literal: The sovereign was moved by the words and changed to erect capital walls.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the prophecy, the emperor rebuilt the capital walls.

sentences.zh: 儉又諫，上答曰：「吾欲令後世無以加也。

translations.literal: Jian remonstrated again; the sovereign answered, 「I wish that later ages have nothing to add.
translations.idiomatic: Jian remonstrated again. The emperor answered, 「I mean for posterity to have nothing left to add.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷初基，制度草創，儉識舊事，問無不答。

translations.literal: 」The court was newly founded and institutions still being created; Jian knew the old affairs and had an answer to every question.
translations.idiomatic: 」The dynasty was still laying its foundations and its rites were only half formed; Jian knew the old precedents and answered every question put to him.

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「《詩》云：『維嶽降神，生甫及申。

translations.literal: The sovereign sighed and said, 「The Odes says: 'The lofty mountain sent down a spirit, and gave birth to Fu and Shen.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, 「The Odes has it: 'From the great mountain came down a spirit, and bore Fu and Shen.'

sentences.zh: 』今亦天爲我生儉也。」

translations.literal: 」Now Heaven has also born Jian for me.」
translations.idiomatic: 」Now Heaven has born Jian for me as well.」

sentences.zh: 其年，儉固請解選，表曰：「臣遠尋終古，近察身事，邀恩幸藉，未見其倫。

translations.literal: That year Jian firmly asked to be relieved of personnel selection, memorializing: 「Your subject, searching far back through antiquity and examining near at hand my own case, have received grace and favor without parallel.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jian firmly asked to lay down the charge of selection and submitted a memorial: 「Your subject, looking far into antiquity and near at my own life, has been showered with grace and favor beyond any parallel I can name.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 子房之遇漢后，公達之逢魏君，史籍以爲美談，君子稱其高義。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang's meeting with the Empress of Han, Sima Yi's encountering the Wei ruler—the histories call these fine tales, gentlemen praise their lofty righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang's service to the Empress of Han, Sima Yi's bond with the Wei sovereign—the histories treat these as fine tales, and gentlemen praise their lofty integrity.

sentences.zh: 二臣才堪王佐，理非曲私，兩主專杖威武，有傷寬裕，豈與庸流之人，憑含弘之澤者，同年而語哉？

translations.literal: Those two ministers were talented enough to aid a king, and in principle were not partial; yet both sovereigns relied solely on awe and might, harming generosity—how can they be spoken of in the same breath as mediocre men who ride the favor of broad forbearance?
translations.idiomatic: Those two ministers had talent fit to aid a throne and were not partial by nature; yet both rulers leaned only on awe and force, wounding magnanimity—how can they be named in one breath with men of the common run who live on an emperor's inclusive grace?

sentences.zh: 預在有心，胡寧無感。

translations.literal: Having shared in their hearts' intent, how could I not be moved?
translations.idiomatic: Having taken part in your purpose of heart, how could I not be stirred?

sentences.zh: 如使傾宗殞元，有益塵露，猶當畢志驅馳，仰詶萬一，豈容稍在形飾，以徇常事。

translations.literal: If by sacrificing my clan and dying I could benefit even as dust or dew, I would still exhaust my will in service and repay a ten-thousandth part—how could I allow myself to linger in outward display for routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If overturning my house and giving my life could profit the state no more than dust or dew, I would still spend myself to the end and repay you one part in ten thousand—how could I linger in outward show for the sake of routine office?

sentences.zh: 九流任要，風猷所先，玉石朱素，由斯而定。

translations.literal: Among the nine ranks, holding the keys is foremost for conduct; jade and stone, red and white—all are fixed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Among the nine currents of office, the keys to appointment come first in shaping conduct; jade and stone, cinnabar and plain—all are sorted by that charge.

sentences.zh: 臣亦不謂文案之間都無微解，至於品裁臧否，特所未閑。

translations.literal: Your subject does not say that among documents there is no slight understanding; but judgment of merit and blame I am quite unversed in.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject does not claim to have no grasp at all of paperwork; but to judge merit and blame is what I truly do not know.

sentences.zh: 雖存自勗，識不副意，兼竊而任，彼此俱壅，專情本官，庶幾髣彿。

translations.literal: Though I urge myself on, my knowledge does not meet my intent; holding two posts at once, both sides are clogged; if I devoted myself only to my primary office, it might barely work.
translations.idiomatic: Though I press myself on, my understanding cannot keep pace with my will; holding two posts at once, both are choked; if I gave my heart only to my chief office, I might barely manage.

sentences.zh: 且前代掌選，未必其在代來，何爲於今，非臣不可。

translations.literal: Moreover those who held selection in former ages were not necessarily from that dynastic house—why now must it be your subject and no other?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover those who held selection in former ages were not always men of the reigning house—why, in our day, must it be your subject and no one else?

sentences.zh: 傾心奉國，匪復退讓之與，預同休戚，寧俟位任爲親。

translations.literal: I devote my heart to serving the state—this is not about yielding rank; sharing weal and woe, why wait on office to be close?
translations.idiomatic: I give my heart to serving the state—that is not a matter of yielding office after office; sharing fortune and peril, why should closeness wait on title and post?

sentences.zh: 陛下若不以此理賜期，豈仰望於殊眷。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not grant this consideration, how could I look to special favor?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not grant this, how could I still look to extraordinary favor?

sentences.zh: 頻冒嚴威，分甘尤戾。

translations.literal: Repeatedly braving your stern dignity, I willingly accept the greater blame.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again I have braved your stern regard; I willingly bear the heavier blame.

sentences.zh: 」見許。

translations.literal: 」Permitted.
translations.idiomatic: 」His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，固讓，復散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was made Palace Attendant; he firmly declined and returned to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Palace Attendant; he firmly declined and remained Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 上曲宴羣臣數人，各使效伎藝，褚淵彈琵琶，王僧虔彈琴，沈文季歌《子夜》，張敬兒舞，王敬則拍張。

translations.literal: The sovereign gave a relaxed banquet for several ministers, each to display a skill: Chu Yuan played pipa, Wang Sengqian played zither, Shen Wenji sang 「Ziye,」 Zhang Jinger danced, Wang Jingze beat the drum.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave an informal banquet for several ministers and had each show a talent: Chu Yuan played pipa, Wang Sengqian the zither, Shen Wenji sang 「Ziye,」 Zhang Jinger danced, and Wang Jingze beat the drum.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「臣無所解，唯知誦書。

translations.literal: Jian said, 「Your subject has no skill—only knows how to recite books.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, 「Your subject has no art—only the recitation of books.

sentences.zh: 」因跪上前誦相如《封禪書》。

translations.literal: 」He then knelt before the throne and recited Sima Xiangru's 「Letter on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices.」
translations.idiomatic: 」He knelt before the throne and recited Sima Xiangru's 「Letter on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices.」

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「此盛德之事，吾何以堪之。

translations.literal: The sovereign smiled and said, 「This is a matter of supreme virtue—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, 「That is an affair of supreme virtue—how could I bear it?

sentences.zh: 」後上使陸澄誦《孝經》，自「仲尼居」而起。

translations.literal: 」Later the sovereign had Lu Cheng recite the Classic of Filial Piety, beginning from 「Zhong Ni dwelt.」
translations.idiomatic: 」Later the emperor had Lu Cheng recite the Classic of Filial Piety, starting from the passage 「Zhong Ni dwelt.」

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「澄所謂博而寡要，臣請誦之。
