translations.literal: Jian said, 「What Cheng offers is broad but lacks essentials—your subject asks to recite.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, 「What Cheng recites is wide but thin at the core—allow your subject to recite instead.

sentences.zh: 」乃誦「《君子之事上》」章。

translations.literal: 」He then recited the chapter 「The Gentleman's Service to His Sovereign.」
translations.idiomatic: 」He then recited the chapter 「The Gentleman's Service to His Sovereign.」

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！

translations.literal: The sovereign said, 「Good!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 「Excellent!

sentences.zh: 張子布更覺非奇也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Zibu seems even less remarkable.」
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zibu seems even less remarkable by comparison.」

sentences.zh: 尋以本官領太子詹事，加兵二百人。

translations.literal: Soon he held his original post as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household with two hundred additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held his existing office while also serving as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, with two hundred additional guards.

sentences.zh: 上崩，遺詔以儉爲侍中、尚書令、鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the sovereign died, the testamentary edict named Jian Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and General Who Stabilizes the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, his testamentary edict named Jian Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and General Who Stabilizes the Army.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，給班劔二十人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu acceded, he was granted twenty halberds of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was granted twenty ceremonial halberds.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，進號衞軍將軍，參掌選事。

translations.literal: In Yongming 1 he was promoted to General of the Guard and shared control of personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 1 he was advanced to General of the Guard and shared charge of selection.

sentences.zh: 二年，領國子祭酒、丹陽尹，本官如故。

translations.literal: In year 2 he also held National University Chancellor and Governor of Danyang, his original posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he also served as National University Chancellor and Governor of Danyang, while keeping his other offices.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was granted one set of ceremonial drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a full set of ceremonial drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 三年，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In year 3 he again held National University Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he again served as National University Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 叔父僧虔亡，儉表解職，不許。

translations.literal: His uncle Sengqian died; Jian memorialized to resign his offices but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Sengqian died, Jian asked to leave office and was refused.

sentences.zh: 又領太子少傅，本州中正，解丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He also became Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and native-place rating chief for this province, and gave up the governorship of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also became Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and chief rating officer for his home province, and resigned as Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 舊太子敬二傅同，至是朝議接少傅以賔友之禮。

translations.literal: Formerly the heir showed equal respect to both tutors; now court deliberation held that the Junior Tutor should be received with guest-and-friend ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the heir had honored both tutors alike; now the court ruled that the Junior Tutor should be received with the rites due a guest and friend.

sentences.zh: 是歲，省總明觀，於儉宅開學士館，悉以四部書充儉家，又詔儉以家爲府。

translations.literal: That year the Zongming Observatory was abolished; at Jian's residence a Scholars' Lodge was opened, and the books of all four divisions were used to fill his house; an edict also made his home a government office.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Zongming Observatory was abolished. At Jian's mansion they opened a Scholars' Lodge and filled his house with books from all four divisions; the court also ordered that his home serve as an official bureau.

sentences.zh: 四年，以本官領吏部。

translations.literal: In year 4 he held his original office while also heading the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he kept his existing posts while also directing the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 儉長禮學，諳究朝儀，每博議，證引先儒，罕有其例。

translations.literal: Jian had long studied ritual; he thoroughly knew court ceremony; in every broad deliberation he cited earlier Confucians—few could match his examples.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had long mastered ritual learning and knew court ceremony through and through. In every broad deliberation he cited the early Confucians—few could offer a parallel.

sentences.zh: 八坐丞郎，無能異者。

translations.literal: None among the Eight Seats' clerks and directors could differ from him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the clerks and directors of the Eight Seats, none could dispute him.

sentences.zh: 令史諮事，賔客滿席，儉應接銓序，傍無留滯。

translations.literal: When clerks came to consult and guests filled the hall, Jian answered them in proper order with nothing left waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks came for consultation and guests packed the hall, Jian received them in proper sequence and left no one waiting.

sentences.zh: 十日一還學，監試諸生，巾卷在庭，劔衞令史儀容甚盛。

translations.literal: Every ten days he returned to the academy, overseeing students' examinations; caps and scrolls filled the courtyard, sword guards and clerks in splendid array.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten days he returned to the academy to oversee the students' examinations. Caps and scrolls filled the courtyard; sword guards and clerks made a splendid show.

sentences.zh: 作解散髻，斜插幘簪，朝野慕之，相與放效。

translations.literal: He wore a loose topknot with a kerchief pin stuck in at a slant; court and countryside admired him and imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a loose, undone topknot with his kerchief pin thrust in at a slant; court and countryside admired him and copied the style.

sentences.zh: 儉常謂人曰：「江左風流宰相，唯有謝安。

translations.literal: Jian often said to people, 「Among the cultivated chancellors south of the Yangtze, only Xie An compares.」
translations.idiomatic: Jian often told people, 「Of the great cultivated ministers who graced the south of the Yangtze, only Xie An stands apart.」

sentences.zh: 」蓋自比也。

translations.literal: It was largely self-comparison.
translations.idiomatic: He was largely measuring himself against that standard.

sentences.zh: 世祖深委仗之，士流選用，奏無不可。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu deeply entrusted affairs to him; for appointments among the gentry elite, no memorial was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu relied on him utterly; for every choice among the leading families, whatever he submitted was approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，卽本號開府儀同三司，固讓。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was given his present title as Equal in Office to the Three Excellencies with an open bureau; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was offered his current rank—Equal in Office to the Three Excellencies with an open bureau—and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 六年，重申前命。

translations.literal: In year 6 the earlier appointment was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the court renewed the earlier appointment.

sentences.zh: 先是詔儉三日一還朝，尚書令史出外諮事，上以往來煩數，復詔儉還尚書下省，月聽十日出外。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had Jian return to court every three days, with Masters of Writing clerks going out to consult him; the emperor, finding the coming and going too frequent, again ordered Jian back to the lower offices of the Masters of Writing, allowing ten days out per month.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had once required Jian at court every three days, with clerks of the Masters of Writing going out to consult him. Finding the traffic too heavy, the emperor ordered him back to the lower offices of the Masters of Writing, with ten days allowed outside each month.

sentences.zh: 儉啓求解選，不許。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized to resign from selection duties; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked in a memorial to be released from personnel selection; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，乃上表曰：「臣比年辭選，具簡天明，款言彰於侍接，丹誠布於朝野，物議不以爲非，聖心未垂矜納。

translations.literal: In year 7 he at last submitted a memorial, saying, 「In recent years I have asked to leave selection duties, laying out my case plainly before Heaven's clarity; sincere words shown in audience, loyal heart spread through court and country. Public opinion does not fault me, yet Your Majesty's heart has not yet shown compassion and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he at last wrote: 「These years I have begged to leave selection—my case set plain before Heaven, honest words in audience, loyal heart known through court and country. No one faults me, yet Your Majesty has not yet shown pity and assent.

sentences.zh: 臣聞知慧不如明時，求之微躬，實允斯義。

translations.literal: I have heard that wisdom is inferior to an enlightened age; to seek that in my humble person truly fits this principle.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that wisdom cannot match a bright age; to look for it in one small man like me truly fits the saying.

sentences.zh: 妄庸之人，沈浮無取，命偶休泰，遂踐康衢。

translations.literal: A mediocre man, adrift without merit, by fate met with a flourishing age and so walked the broad road.
translations.idiomatic: A shallow man, drifting without worth, by luck met a golden age and walked the wide road.

sentences.zh: 秋葉辭條，不假風飆之力；

translations.literal: Autumn leaves leave the branch without needing the storm's force;
translations.idiomatic: Autumn leaves fall from the branch without waiting on the gale;

sentences.zh: 太陽躋景，無俟螢爝之暉。

translations.literal: the sun climbs to its glory without waiting for a firefly's gleam.
translations.idiomatic: the sun climbs to noon without borrowing a firefly's light.

sentences.zh: 晦往明來，五德遞運，聖不獨治，八元亮采。

translations.literal: Dark gives way to light; the five phases rotate in turn. The sage does not rule alone—the eight worthy ones display their colors.
translations.idiomatic: Dark yields to bright; the five virtues turn in season. The sage does not govern alone—the eight worthies bring forth their light.

sentences.zh: 臣逢其時，而叨其位，常總端右，亟管銓衡。

translations.literal: I met that season and yet hold such rank, constantly presiding at the chief seat, repeatedly managing the scales of selection.
translations.idiomatic: I met that hour and yet hold this place, always at the head of the court, again and again at the scales of appointment.

sentences.zh: 事涉兩朝，歲綿一紀。

translations.literal: Matters span two reigns; years stretch a full twelve-year cycle.
translations.idiomatic: My service spans two reigns; the years run a full cycle.

sentences.zh: 盛年已老，孫孺巾冠。

translations.literal: My flourishing years have turned old; grandchildren wear caps.
translations.idiomatic: My prime has turned old; grandsons and granddaughters wear their caps.

sentences.zh: 人物徂遷，逝者將半。

translations.literal: Men and affairs pass away; half are already gone.
translations.idiomatic: Men and things shift away; half the known world is already gone.

sentences.zh: 三考無聞，九流寂寞。

translations.literal: The three reviews bring no renown; the nine streams lie silent.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds of assessment win no praise; the nine currents stand empty.

sentences.zh: 能官之詠，輟響於當時；

translations.literal: The praise of able ministers has ceased in this age;
translations.idiomatic: The song of able ministers has fallen silent in our time;

sentences.zh: 《大車》之刺，方興於來日。

translations.literal: the satire of "Great Chariot" is rising for days to come.
translations.idiomatic: the sting of "Great Chariot" is rising for the days ahead.

sentences.zh: 若夫珥貂衣袞之貴，四輔六教之華，誠知匪服，職務差簡，端揆雖重，猶可勉勵。

translations.literal: As for the honor of wearing the finned cap and court robes, the splendor of the four aides and six ministries—I know I am unworthy, those duties are somewhat lighter, and though the chief minister's post is weighty, one might still strive at it.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rank of finned cap and dragon robe, the glory of the four pillars and six ministries—I know I am unfit, those tasks are lighter, and though the head of state is heavy, one might still try.

sentences.zh: 至於品藻之任，尤懼其阻。

translations.literal: But the task of judging character and rank—I fear above all that I block it.
translations.idiomatic: But the work of judging men and ranks—that above all I fear I choke.

sentences.zh: 夙宵罄竭，屢試無庸。

translations.literal: I exhaust myself night and day, try again and again, yet prove useless.
translations.idiomatic: Night and day I spend myself; again and again I am tried, and again found wanting.

sentences.zh: 歲月之久，近世罕比。

translations.literal: Such a length of years—in recent times scarcely matched.
translations.idiomatic: So long in the post—in recent memory there is no like case.

sentences.zh: 非唯悔吝在身，故乃惟塵及國。

translations.literal: Not only regret and shame cling to my person—it brings dust upon the state as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shame is not mine alone; dust settles on the realm as well.

sentences.zh: 方今多士盈朝，羣才競爽，選衆而授，古亦何人。

translations.literal: Now the court brims with scholars; talents vie in brightness. To choose from the many and appoint—who in antiquity was such a man?
translations.idiomatic: Today the court overflows with talent; men compete in brilliance. To pick from the crowd and entrust office—who in old times was equal to that?

sentences.zh: 冒陳微翰，必希天照。

translations.literal: I dare set forth this slight letter, hoping surely for Heaven's illumination.
translations.idiomatic: I dare offer this poor letter, trusting in Heaven's light.

sentences.zh: 至敬無文，不敢煩黷。

translations.literal: Utmost respect needs no ornament; I dare not trouble you with further words.
translations.idiomatic: The deepest reverence needs no flourish; I dare not weary you further.

sentences.zh: 」見許。

translations.literal: 」 It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: 」 The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 改領中書監，參掌選事。

translations.literal: He was changed to concurrently hold Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, still sharing selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, still sharing charge of selection.

sentences.zh: 其年疾，上親臨視，薨，年三十八。

translations.literal: That year he fell ill; the emperor personally visited him. He died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: That year he sickened; the emperor came in person to his bedside. He died at thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王晏啓及儉喪，上答曰：「儉年德富盛，志用方隆，豈意暴疾，不展救護，便爲異世，奄忽如此，痛酷彌深。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, Minister of the Masters of Personnel, memorialized on Jian's death. The emperor replied, 「Jian's years and virtue were in fullest flower, his ambition and use just rising—who could have thought a sudden illness, with no scope for healing, would place him in another world so abruptly? The pain is unbearably deep.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel, wrote on Jian's death. The emperor answered: 「Jian's years and virtue stood at their height, his will and work just ascending—who could have thought a sudden sickness, with no room for cure, would cast him so quickly into another world? The pain cuts unbearably deep.

sentences.zh: 其契闊艱運，義重常懷，言尋悲切，不能自勝。

translations.literal: His trials through hard fates, his constant weight of right feeling—to speak of them is grief that cuts; I cannot master myself.
translations.idiomatic: His shared trials through hard times, the weight of right feeling I always bore—to speak of it is grief I cannot hold in.

sentences.zh: 痛矣奈何！

translations.literal: Pain—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: Pain—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 往矣奈何！

translations.literal: Gone—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: Gone—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 」詔衞軍文武及臺所兵仗可悉停待葬。

translations.literal: 」 Edict: All civil and military officers of the Guard General and all central-office arms and equipment shall halt until the burial.
translations.idiomatic: 」 An edict ordered all civil and military staff of the Guard General and all arms of the central offices to stand idle until the burial.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「慎終追遠，列代通規，褒德紀勳，彌峻恒策。

translations.literal: Another edict read, 「To care for the end and reach back to the distant is the common rule of every age; to praise virtue and record merit is the ever-stricter constant policy.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: 「To tend the dead and honor the distant is the rule of every dynasty; to praise virtue and record merit is the policy that grows only stricter.

sentences.zh: 故侍中、中書令、太子少傅、領國子祭酒、衞軍將軍、開府儀同三司南昌公儉，體道秉哲，風宇淵曠。

translations.literal: The late Palace Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Chancellor of the Imperial University, Guard General, Equal in Office to the Three Excellencies with open bureau, Duke of Nanchang Jian embodied the Way and held wisdom; his bearing was deep and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The late Palace Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Chancellor of the Imperial University, Guard General, Equal in Office to the Three Excellencies with open bureau, Duke of Nanchang Jian—he held the Way and wisdom, his presence deep and wide.

sentences.zh: 肇自弱齡，清猷自遠。

translations.literal: From tender years his pure design reached afar.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood his clear purpose reached far.

sentences.zh: 登朝應務，民望斯屬。

translations.literal: When he entered court and took up affairs, the people's hopes rested on him.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered court and bore office, the people's hopes turned to him.

sentences.zh: 草昧皇基，協隆鼎祚；

translations.literal: In the founding of the royal foundation he helped raise the royal mandate;
translations.idiomatic: In the rough founding of the throne he helped lift the royal mandate;

sentences.zh: 宏謨盛烈，載銘彝篆。

translations.literal: great designs and splendid deeds, recorded on ritual bronze.
translations.idiomatic: great plans and shining deeds, cut into the ritual bronze.

sentences.zh: 及贊朕躬，徽績光茂。

translations.literal: When he aided Our person, his fine merit shone bright.
translations.idiomatic: When he aided Our person, his fine merit blazed.

sentences.zh: 忠圖令範，造次必彰。

translations.literal: Loyal counsel and fine models—in every moment they showed.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal design and worthy example—in every act they showed.

sentences.zh: 四門允穆，百揆時序。

translations.literal: The four gates were harmonious; the hundred offices kept order.
translations.idiomatic: The four gates stood in peace; the hundred offices kept their seasons.

sentences.zh: 宗臣之重，情寄兼常。

translations.literal: As a weighty clan minister, his trust joined kin and state.
translations.idiomatic: As a great minister of the clan, his bond joined house and realm.

sentences.zh: 方正位論道，永釐袞職，弼茲景化，以贊隆平。

translations.literal: He was to stand in rectitude and discuss the Way, forever set the imperial robe in order, assist this bright transformation, and help the age of peace and abundance.
translations.idiomatic: He was to stand upright and speak the Way, forever set the royal robe straight, brace this bright age, and help the time of peace and plenty.

sentences.zh: 天不憖遺，奄焉薨逝，朕用震慟于厥心。

translations.literal: Heaven was not kind; suddenly he passed away. We are shaken and grief-stricken in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was unkind; suddenly he was gone. We are shaken with grief in Our heart.

sentences.zh: 可追贈太尉，侍中、中書監、公如故。

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously granted Grand Commandant, Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, duke as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted posthumously: Grand Commandant, Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, duke as before.

sentences.zh: 給節，加羽葆鼓吹，增班劔爲六十人。

translations.literal: Grant insignia, add feather-canopy drums and pipes, increase guard swords to sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Give insignia, add feather-canopy band and drums, raise his guard of honor swords to sixty.

sentences.zh: 葬禮依故太宰文簡公褚淵故事。

translations.literal: Funeral rites per the precedent of the late Grand Preceptor, Duke Wenjian Chu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral follows the precedent of the late Grand Preceptor, Duke Wenjian Chu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 冢墓材官營辦。

translations.literal: The tomb and grave to be prepared by the engineering corps.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb and grave shall be built by the engineering troops.

sentences.zh: 謚文憲公。」

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wenxian Duke.」
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke Wenxian.」

sentences.zh: 儉寡嗜慾，唯以經國爲務，車服塵素，家無遺財。

translations.literal: Jian was frugal and had few desires; he devoted himself only to ordering the state. His carriage and dress were plain and dusty; the household left no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Jian lived sparely, with few wants, and gave himself only to governing the realm. His carriage and robes were plain; when he died the house held no spare wealth.

sentences.zh: 手筆典裁，爲當時所重。

translations.literal: His own brush in canonical composition was valued in his time.
translations.idiomatic: What he wrote with his own hand—memorials and literary pieces—was prized throughout his age.

sentences.zh: 少撰《古今喪服集記》幷文集，並行於世。

translations.literal: In youth he compiled the Collection of Mourning Garments, Ancient and Modern, and a collected literary works; both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: While young he compiled the Collection of Mourning Garments, Ancient and Modern, and a collected literary works; both were in wide circulation.

sentences.zh: 今上受禪，下詔爲儉立碑，降爵爲侯，千戶。

translations.literal: When the present sovereign received the Mandate, an edict ordered a stele erected for Jian, the rank lowered to marquis, one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor took the Mandate, he issued an edict to raise a stele for Jian, lowered the enfeoffment to marquis, and granted a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 儉弟遜，昇明中，爲丹陽丞，告劉秉事，不蒙封賞。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Xun, in the Shengming era, was assistant magistrate of Danyang; he reported Liu Bing's affair and received no enfeoffment or reward.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Xun, in the Shengming period, was assistant magistrate of Danyang. He informed on Liu Bing's plot and won neither fief nor reward.

sentences.zh: 建元初，爲晉陵太守，有怨言，儉慮爲禍，因褚淵啓聞。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyuan he was Administrator of Jinling; he uttered resentful words. Jian feared disaster and, through Chu Yuan, reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyuan he was Administrator of Jinling and let fall bitter words. Jian feared he would bring ruin and had Chu Yuan lay the matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 中丞陸澄依事舉奏。

translations.literal: Vice Censor Lu Cheng submitted impeachment according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor Lu Cheng impeached him on the facts of the case.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「儉門世載德，竭誠佐命，特降刑書，宥遜以遠。

translations.literal: An edict said: 「Jian's line has borne virtue for generations and served the mandate with utter devotion; we specially moderate the criminal writ and spare Xun by exile afar.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 「Jian's house has carried virtue for generations and given the throne his whole loyalty; we therefore temper the sentence of law and spare Xun by banishment to a distant place.

sentences.zh: 」徙永嘉郡，道伏誅。

translations.literal: 」He was transferred to Yongjia commandery; on the road he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was sent to Yongjia commandery and was put to death on the way.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：褚淵、袁粲，俱受宋明帝顧託，粲旣死節於宋氏，而淵逢興運，世之非責淵者衆矣。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Chu Yuan and Yuan Can both received Emperor Ming of Song's deathbed entrustment. Can already died in loyalty for the Song house, while Yuan met the rising fortune—many in the world blame Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Chu Yuan and Yuan Can both received Emperor Ming of Song's deathbed charge. Can died in loyalty to the Song house; Yuan met the rising fortune—and the world has been quick to blame him.

sentences.zh: 臣請論之：夫湯、武之迹，異乎堯、舜，伊、呂之心，亦非稷、契。

translations.literal: Your subject begs to discuss it: The tracks of Tang and Wu differ from those of Yao and Shun; the hearts of Yi Yin and Tai Gong are not those of Hou Ji and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Let me argue the point: Tang and Wu walked a different path from Yao and Shun; the hearts of Yi Yin and Tai Gong were not those of Hou Ji and Qi.

sentences.zh: 降此風規，未足爲證也。

translations.literal: To lower this standard of conduct is not enough to serve as proof.
translations.idiomatic: To judge by that lower measure of conduct is no fair ground for blame.

sentences.zh: 自金、張世族，袁、楊鼎貴，委質服義，皆由漢氏，膏腴見重，事起於斯。

translations.literal: From the Jin and Zhang great clans, Yuan and Yang at the height of honor—all submitted in loyalty through the Han house; fertile domains won esteem, and the matter began there.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin and Zhang lines, the Yuan and Yang houses at the summit of rank—each pledged service and loyalty under the Han; fertile estates were prized, and the custom took root there.

sentences.zh: 魏氏君臨，年祚短促，服褐前代，宦成後朝。

translations.literal: When Wei ruled, its reign was brief; they wore coarse cloth for the former dynasty and won office under the later court.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei held the throne its years were few; men still wore the brown of the former house even as they finished their careers under the court that followed.

sentences.zh: 晉氏登庸，與之從事，名雖魏臣，實爲晉有，故主位雖改，臣任如初。

translations.literal: When the Jin house ascended to office, they went on in its service; though in name they were ministers of Wei, in fact they belonged to Jin—so though the sovereign's seat changed, a minister's charge remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin took the throne they went on in its service; on paper they were Wei's ministers, in truth they were Jin's men—so though the ruler changed, the minister's post stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 自是世祿之盛，習爲舊準，羽儀所隆，人懷羨慕，君臣之節，徒致虛名。

translations.literal: From this the splendor of hereditary stipends became the old standard; what regalia honored, men envied—the bond of lord and minister was reduced to an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary wealth became the fixed pattern; men coveted whatever the panoply exalted—loyalty between lord and minister was loyalty in name only.

sentences.zh: 貴仕素資，皆由門慶，平流進取，坐至公卿，則知殉國之感無因，保家之念宜切。

translations.literal: Qualifications for high office all rested on family glory; riding the common stream of advancement, one sat till he reached minister or grandee—thus one sees there was no ground for dying for the state, and the wish to preserve the clan ought to have been keen.
translations.idiomatic: Rank came from pedigree; riding the ordinary tide of promotion, men took their seats among the Three Dukes without stir—so zeal to die for the state had no foothold, and guarding the clan should have weighed more.

sentences.zh: 市朝亟革，寵貴方來，陵闕雖殊，顧眄如一。

translations.literal: Court and market changed again and again; favor and rank newly arrived; though tombs and palaces differed, the backward glance was still one.
translations.idiomatic: Thrones turned over fast; new favor and new dignity arrived—though dynastic tombs and palaces changed, the look cast backward was the same.

sentences.zh: 中行、智伯，未有異遇。

translations.literal: Not even Zhonghang or Zhibo received different treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhonghang and Zhibo would have found no special treatment.

sentences.zh: 褚淵當泰始初運，清塗已顯，數年之閒，不患無位，旣以民望而見引，亦隨民望而去之。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan, at the opening of the Taishi fortune, already stood on a clear path; within a few years he need not fear lacking office—brought forward by popular acclaim, he also withdrew as popular acclaim willed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan at the rise of Taishi was already on a bright track; within a few years he need not fear lacking a post—lifted by public renown, he also left as public renown turned.

sentences.zh: 夫爵祿旣輕，有國常選，恩非己獨，責人以死，斯故人主之所同謬，世情之過差也。

translations.literal: When rank and stipend are already light, the state has its regular choice; favor is not his alone—yet men are charged to die for it. This is a common error of rulers and an excess of the age's sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: When titles and stipends weigh little and the realm chooses by rule, when the grace is not his alone yet men are asked to die for it—that is a mistake rulers commonly make and a bias the age runs to.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：猗歟褚公，德素內充。

translations.literal: In praise: How grand Lord Chu! Plain virtue filled within.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: O Lord Chu, how great! Plain virtue brimmed within.

sentences.zh: 民譽不爽，家稱克隆。

translations.literal: The people's praise never missed; the clan was called abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Popular esteem never faltered; the house was held to flourish.

sentences.zh: 從容佐世，貽議匪躬。

translations.literal: At ease aiding his age, he left censure not confined to himself.
translations.idiomatic: With ease he aided his times; blame he drew did not stop at his person alone.

sentences.zh: 文憲濟濟，輔相之體。

translations.literal: Civil and canonical, full in stature—the bearing of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Cultured and law-giving, stately and full—the mold of a chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 稱述霸王，綱維典禮。

translations.literal: He proclaimed the hegemons and kings; he held the warp of rites and norms.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth the model of sage rule; he held the threads of ritual and statute.

sentences.zh: 期寄兩朝，綢繆宮陛。

translations.literal: Trusted across two reigns, bound close at the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted through two reigns, intimate at the palace threshold.
